title: Learning of Population Dynamics: Inverse Optimization Meets JKO Scheme
claim: Learn dynamics by minimizing the gap between optimal objective values under the model and suboptimal values at ground-truth states.
layout: 1 panel, 3D-style manifold with trajectories, vertical level curves, callout boxes
description: A single perspective illustration of a purple Wasserstein-2 space, drawn as a blob-shaped manifold. Two trajectories run across it. A solid mauve curve is the true evolution through ρ0, ρ1 and ρ2. A dotted navy curve is the predicted evolution, ending at the points ρ̂1(θ) and ρ̂2(θ). Thin vertical gray lines rise from each point as JKO objective level curves. On them, red ellipses mark optimal objective values and yellow ellipses mark suboptimal values at the ground-truth points. Dashed arrows lead up to these ellipses, and a gradient-shaded strip between each pair shows the gap. A gray box labeled 'Inverse JKO loss' points at the gaps. A blue box shows the JKO functional J_θ(·) + (1/2τ)d²(ρ_{k-1}, ·). A legend sits at top left, and the 'W2 space' label sits at right.
caption: iJKOnet working scheme: our method minimizes the gap between the optimal values of parametric (θ) JKO functional and suboptimal values obtained at ground truth population measures.
abstract: Learning population dynamics involves recovering the underlying process that governs particle evolution, given evolutionary snapshots of samples at discrete time points. Recent methods frame this as an energy minimization problem in probability space and leverage the celebrated JKO scheme for efficient time discretization. In this work, we introduce $\texttt{iJKOnet}$, an approach that combines the JKO framework with inverse optimization techniques to learn population dynamics. Our method relies on a conventional $\textit{end-to-end}$ adversarial training procedure and does not require restrictive architectural choices, e.g., input-convex neural networks. We establish theoretical guarantees for our methodology and demonstrate improved performance over prior JKO-based methods. The code of $\texttt{iJKOnet}$ is available at https://github.com/MuXauJl11110/iJKOnet.
